prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Editorial photograph for a top Scandinavian interiors magazine: a long quiet corridor in a Nordic garden house, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.2 m, level, one-point symmetric, vanishing point at the centre, all sharp. Hero: a gallery of light, the left wall washed from a slot in the ceiling, leading the eye to the glowing hall and living room at the end.

2. LIGHT. No window. A continuous frosted roof slot along the top of the left wall is the key: soft top light that washes the left wall, brightest under the ceiling and softening toward the floor, with a gentle gradient along its length. Exposed for that wall: it reads clean warm white, just under the glowing slot; the vista at the end one step brighter and still detailed: the oak portal, the hall console, the living room beyond. The right wall with its doors sits in soft shade. Each object has a lit upper-left face and a darker side, feathered shadows down and to the right, short contact shadows. The dropped ceiling a touch darker than the walls, darkest at the top right. No sun patch. White balance 4600 K: warm white, never pink, yellow or grey; real contrast, never milky. Practicals 2700 K, low, no shadows: the paper lanterns glow evenly from within, and the far one lays a faint warm pool on the floor below it.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC, faint chalky movement in the raking light. Flush doors in the wall colour, matte black levers. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E, running the whole length, with a soft satin sheen: one long soft highlight down the planks toward the hall; no mirror reflection. The oak portal at the end: oiled oak #C8A27A.

4. PRODUCTS, exactly these:
a. GALLERY on the left wall, x 0.19-0.35: three 40 x 40 framed prints in a row, 20 cm apart, centres at 1.45 m, each a calm black ink brushstroke abstract on cream inside a very wide warm-white mat, thin matte black aluminium frame, no glass and no glare; each print a little under half a door's width; all three share one top line.
b. CEILING: two flat oval rice-paper lanterns, 40 wide and 22 high, warm white, on short cords close to the ceiling, lit; the far one fully visible at x 0.50, y 0.13, about as wide as one print; the near one above the frame.
c. THE VISTA shows only its own rooms' products: in the hall a framed black line print over an oak console with a white ceramic vase and a black oval tray; beyond, the living room's prints, sofa and glowing lamps.

5. NOT IN FRAME: picture lights, runner or rug, stool, bench, plants, anything on the right wall or doors, shoes, books, mirror, glass, cable, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, glow halos, HDR look, grain or vignette.
